podcast.title: Life in 1977
podcast.body: In 1977, just two years before her debut album, Ricky Lee Jones experienced a period of personal hardship. She recalled having few friends, no stable place to live, and very little money. "She said she didn't have many friends. She didn't have a place to live. She didn't have any money."

podcast.title: Perception of The Troubadour in 1978
podcast.body: By 1978, Ricky Lee Jones characterized The Troubadour as "a club for used to be singers," and observed it was "mostly an empty club," reflecting its decline from its earlier legendary status as a hub for emerging artists. "By 1978, the troubadour was as Ricky Lee Jones put it, it used to be club for used to be singers."

podcast.title: Grammy for Best New Artist (1980)
podcast.body: In 1980, Ricky Lee Jones won the Grammy for Best New Artist. She competed against notable acts such as The Blues Brothers, The Knack, Robin Williams, and Dire Straits for the award. "And then in 1980, Ricky Lee Jones won a Grammy for Best New Artist."

podcast.title: First Troubadour Performance and Key Meetings
podcast.body: Jones made her debut at The Troubadour when a friend who was performing there asked her to sing a couple of songs. It was there that she met Chuck Weiss, who was working in the club's kitchen, and later Tom Waits, leading to the three of them hanging out and forming a significant, though turbulent, relationship with Waits. "A guy she knew was performing at the troubadour and he asked her to go over there and sing a couple of songs."
